columnPool.label: Route: Great Eastern Main Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Great Eastern Main Line route
columnPool.hint: The core trunk route from London Liverpool Street via Colchester and Ipswich to Norwich - the main line the other Essex/Suffolk/Norfolk branches all connect into.

columnPool.label: Route: Great Eastern
columnPool.display: Is part of the Great Eastern route
columnPool.hint: The wider network of lines radiating from London Liverpool Street across Essex, Suffolk and Norfolk - a broader grouping than just the Great Eastern Main Line trunk route itself.

columnPool.label: Route: Heron Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Heron Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from London Liverpool Street via Bishop's Stortford, Audley End and Shelford to Cambridge - the slower, more-stops alternative to the direct Cambridge fasts.

columnPool.label: Route: West Anglia Main Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the West Anglia Main Line route
columnPool.hint: The main line north from London Liverpool Street through Tottenham Hale, Broxbourne and Bishop's Stortford to Cambridge - the other of the two main lines out of Liverpool Street, alongside the Great Eastern Main Line.

columnPool.label: Route: West Anglia
columnPool.display: Is part of the West Anglia route
columnPool.hint: The wider network of lines radiating from Liverpool Street north through Essex and Hertfordshire - including the Stansted Airport and Hertford East branches, not just the core West Anglia Main Line.

columnPool.label: Route: London Tilbury & Southend Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the London Tilbury & Southend Line route
columnPool.hint: The historic name for c2c's own route from London Fenchurch Street via Tilbury to Southend - a separate corridor from Greater Anglia's Shenfield-Southend line.

columnPool.label: Route: East Suffolk Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the East Suffolk Line route
columnPool.hint: The rural single-track line from Ipswich via Saxmundham to Lowestoft, with a branch to Felixstowe - one of the longest and least direct routes in East Anglia.

columnPool.label: Route: Sunshine Coast Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Sunshine Coast Line route
columnPool.hint: The branch from Colchester to the Essex seaside resorts of Clacton-on-Sea and Walton-on-the-Naze - officially rebranded with this name for its coastal tourist appeal.

columnPool.label: Route: Mayflower Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Mayflower Line route
columnPool.hint: The short branch from Manningtree to Harwich, named for the Mayflower's historic sailing connection to the town.

columnPool.label: Route: Shenfield to Southend Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Shenfield to Southend Line route
columnPool.hint: The Great Eastern branch south from Shenfield through Wickford to Southend Victoria - same route as the Southend Line, just described more literally by its endpoints.

columnPool.label: Route: Southend Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Southend Line route
columnPool.hint: The Great Eastern branch south from Shenfield through Wickford to Southend Victoria - also called the Shenfield to Southend Line.

columnPool.label: Route: St Edmund's Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the St Edmund's Line route
columnPool.hint: The route from Ipswich via Bury St Edmunds and Newmarket to Cambridge - named after Saint Edmund, King of the East Angles, following a 2026 public naming competition.

columnPool.label: Route: Wherry Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Wherry Line route
columnPool.hint: The route east from Norwich to the coast at Great Yarmouth and Lowestoft, named after the traditional Norfolk Broads sailing boats.

columnPool.label: Route: Hertford East Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Hertford East Line route
columnPool.hint: The branch off the Lea Valley Lines that continues north to Hertford East - closely linked with the Lee Valley Line, which covers the shared stem through Cheshunt and Broxbourne.

columnPool.label: Route: Lee Valley Line
columnPool.display: Is part of the Lee Valley Line route
columnPool.hint: The suburban route north from London through the Lea Valley via Cheshunt and Broxbourne, continuing on the Hertford East branch - closely linked with the Hertford East Line.
